messages:
leo: FYI escalation from ACME on their Private VPC deployment — they see intermittent 403s on inference API and then some worker nodes making outbound TLS connections to analytics.partner.com. They also say KMS decrypt audit logs are missing for those requests. We need quick triage.

acme-cse: customer reported incidents at ~2026-03-11T10:12Z; provided this firewall snapshot and host logs. They expect egress locked to internal endpoints only.

maria: can you paste the VPC id + a short snippet of the node iptables / security-group rules? also cloud provider + region.

leo: VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d, region us-west-2. Node pool cluster-17, workers in subnet 10.40.2.0/24. Provided iptables excerpt:
```
# iptables -S
-P INPUT ACCEPT
-P FORWARD DROP
-P OUTPUT ACCEPT
-A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
-A OUTPUT -d 10.0.0.0/8 -j ACCEPT
```
They said the intent was to have a restrictive egress rule (only 10.40.0.0/16 + our private registry), but policy showed generic allow 443 which opened to internet.

simon: if OUTPUT policy is ACCEPT and there's a broad --dport 443 rule, that'll let nodes egress to external hosts. Does the customer run our node-agent that enforces policy? Any network policy CRs applied?

acme-cse: they are running our node-agent v1.9.1, but the cluster had a manual change during onboarding. They attached agent logs showing connection attempts then KMS errors:
```
2026-03-11T10:11:57Z host-agent[2378]: kms-client: request id=.. failed: dial tcp 52.23.11.7:443: i/o timeout
2026-03-11T10:12:02Z host-agent[2378]: auth: token refresh 401, retrying
2026-03-11T10:12:05Z host-agent[2378]: inference: request id=.. -> fallback model (auth error)
```
No kms:Decrypt events in their CloudWatch audit stream for the same timeframe.

tess: two threads here — 1) firewall misconfiguration allowing egress; 2) missing KMS logs. For KMS, ask whether they use a customer-managed CMK vs cloud-managed key and whether logs ship to a different account/region. For firewall: reproduce via tcpdump to see destination SNI.

maria: agreed. Steps to triage (quick):
- confirm CMK ARN + key policy and CloudTrail region for KMS events
- check VPC Flow Logs for TCP/443 ACCEPT entries from node IPs to analytics.partner.com IPs
- run `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/egress.pcap tcp port 443` for 60s on an affected node
- dump iptables `iptables-save` and k8s NetworkPolicy resources

leo: ran the flow logs query (customer provided): small excerpt ->
```
10.40.2.11 34.200.12.9 443 6 ACCEPT 60 2026-03-11T10:12:01Z
10.40.2.12 52.23.11.7 443 6 ACCEPT 40 2026-03-11T10:12:02Z
```
The analytics.partner.com resolved to 34.200.12.9 and 52.23.11.7.

simon: that matches agent logs. KMS timeout (dial tcp) indicates egress to KMS endpoint failed while egress to analytics succeeded — implies some routing/nat or proxy rule preventing reachability to regional KMS while allowing internet egress. Is there a NAT gateway with endpoint policy?

acme-cse: customer says they have an interface endpoint for KMS in the subnet (com.amazonaws.kms) but endpoint health reported as 'available'. No obvious route table changes.

tess: check host-level resolver and /etc/hosts, maybe KMS endpoint resolved to private IP that routes to a misconfigured proxy. Also verify ENI security groups attached to the interface endpoint — SG could block our node's SG.

maria: good call. Also confirm CloudTrail data event configuration: if CloudTrail isn't configured to log management events for KMS in that region, there will be no kms:Decrypt events. Ask customer to run: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2026-03-11T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-12T00:00:00Z`

leo: customer ran the CloudTrail command -> returned zero results. They send a screenshot: CloudTrail is enabled but only for S3 data events, not management events for KMS. They thought CloudWatch KMS logs were always on.

simon: root causes likely: 1) overly permissive iptables/egress rules allowed outbound to analytics; 2) KMS management events not configured in CloudTrail so there is no audit trail; 3) KMS timeouts possibly caused by SG or proxy routing to wrong endpoint.

maria: next actions (assign):
- leo: apply temporary egress block for nodes to 0.0.0.0/0:443 (deny) and allow only required endpoints (10.40.0.0/16 + registry + kms endpoint IPs) — we should coordinate with customer for brief maintenance window.
- acme-cse: enable CloudTrail management events for KMS in us-west-2 and re-run lookup.
- simon: help the customer check ENI/SG for KMS interface endpoint and run `curl -v https://kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/` from node to see TLS handshake IP.
- tess: prepare a short post-incident note explaining audit-gap and recommended hardening (restrict egress, enforce network policy, require CloudTrail KMS logging, verify endpoint SGs).

deploy-bot: applied change request cr-9912 -> egress rule update scheduled at 2026-03-11T10:32Z (maintenance window).

acme-cse: customer approves maintenance window. They will enable CloudTrail management events now and will share results.

leo: I ran `curl -v https://kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/` from node-3 and saw it resolve to 10.10.5.23 (private IP) and connection timed out. That ENI SG was only allowing port 443 from a different service account than our nodes. reassigning to simon to coordinate SG change.

simon: thanks — I'll request permission change on endpoint SG rules and then help verify KMS logs once CloudTrail is enabled. We should also add an automated onboarding check to validate CloudTrail management events and restrictive egress rules for future Private deployments.

maria: documenting the triage and next steps in the incident tracker. If anyone has additional quick repro snippets, paste here. :thumbsup:
